subject: Request: US-only processing + VPC routing for HIPAA workloads
messages:
From: Daria Ivanova <daria@medixhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medixhealth.com>, Medix Health Legal <legal@medixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: US-only processing + VPC routing for HIPAA workloads

Mina,

Thanks for taking this. Medix is preparing to push Redwood-backed inference into our production PHI flow for a pilot next quarter. Before procurement will sign a PO, security and legal need a few firm commitments and evidence items: 

- A contractual commitment that all Medix PHI will be processed and stored exclusively in US-based infrastructure (no EU/APAC egress).
- Confirmation that customer traffic can be steered via VPC peering (private connector) to a dedicated constrained path and that we can restrict egress to US-only subnets.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II (redacted ok), a high-level VPC/network diagram showing routing controls, and KMS region details (are customer keys stored in US-region KMS/HSM?).
- Any impact to latency/cost if we require US-only routing and VPC-only ingress (we need a ballpark).

Attached: Medix_Security_Q.pdf (our questionnaire with checkboxes for vendor answers).

Can you confirm Redwood can provide written contractual language for the US-only processing commitment (we can add as an addendum to the BAA) and an estimated delivery timeline? Procurement would like to close by mid-October.

Thanks,
Daria
Director, Security & Compliance
Medix Health
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Daria Ivanova <daria@medixhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@medixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-02T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: US-only processing + VPC routing for HIPAA workloads

Daria —

Appreciate the clear list. We can support a US-only processing commitment for Medix and are able to present a VPC-based routing approach that constrains egress to US-only subnets. High level answers up front:

- Contractual commitment: yes — we can provide addendum language to the BAA that specifies processing will occur only in US regions and that Redwood will not transfer or route PHI outside the US. I'll loop in Legal to draft the wording.
- VPC routing: we support Private Connector (VPC peering) and can configure routing policies and egress filters to restrict outbound traffic to designated US subnets.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II (summary + redacted report) and a VPC architecture diagram can be provided. Customer-managed KMS keys are supported; we can confirm region placement in the US.
- Cost/latency impact: there may be slight cost delta for dedicated routing and pinned capacity; I will ask Dev for a ballpark. Latency should remain in single-digit additional ms unless you require reserved Dedicated capacity.

Next steps:
1) I'll have Legal draft addendum language and send it by EOD.
2) Share SOC2 summary + network diagram and KMS confirmation.
3) Schedule a 30-min technical sync with your infra team to walk the diagram.

Would tomorrow 10:00am PT work for the technical sync?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Mina / Team,

Draft language below for the BAA addendum to capture the US-only processing commitment. This is intentionally concise and scoped to Medix's pilot. We can expand if they request broader terms.

--- DRAFT BAA ADDENDUM LANGUAGE ---
1) Data Residency Commitment: Redwood Inference shall process, store, and transmit Protected Health Information (PHI) related to Medix Health exclusively within infrastructure located in the United States. Redwood shall not transfer or permit transfer of Medix PHI outside the United States except as required by law, in which case Redwood shall notify Medix promptly.

2) Routing Controls; VPC Peering: Where Medix elects to use Redwood's Private Connector (VPC peering) or equivalent private routing mechanism, Redwood shall implement routing policies and egress filtering to restrict outbound traffic for Medix's tenant to designated US-only subnets.

3) Subprocessors: Redwood shall ensure any subcontractors engaged to process Medix PHI are contractually bound to the same US-only processing obligations or will operate within US-only infrastructure for the benefit of Medix.

4) Exceptions & Fallback: In the event of sustained unavailability of US-based capacity that prevents compliance with the US-only commitment, Redwood shall (a) notify Medix, (b) provide remediation options and timelines, and (c) seek Medix's prior written consent before executing any temporary cross-border processing.

--- end draft ---

Rachel here — from an evidence checklist perspective we should provide:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) or SOC 2 summary + auditor letter
- High-level VPC architecture diagram showing peering, route tables, and egress filter points
- Confirmation of KMS support and region placement for customer-managed keys
- Scoped statement on subprocessors (list or attestation)

I recommend we also produce an internal ops attestation (one-paragraph) signed by the Infra owner confirming our ability to enforce egress filters at the tenant level. Markus — can your team produce that attestation and the diagram? Dev — cost/latency estimate here please.

I'll prepare the addendum and circulate for sign-off.

Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround and draft language. A few clarifying asks before we loop procurement: 

- SOC 2: A redacted SOC 2 Type II report is preferred. If not available, provide an auditor attestation and a controls summary.
- KMS: We need confirmation that customer-managed keys can be provisioned and stored in the US region(s) you list and whether keys are exportable.
- VPC diagram: please include the exact route table entries and the enforcement point where egress filtering is applied (gateway vs. tenant agent).
- Subprocessors: list any subprocessors that will see data or the attestation if none outside the US.
- Timeline: procurement needs final addendum and evidence by 2026-10-15 to meet our internal launch windows. Doable?

Also, can you provide a short note on how Redwood will demonstrate operational control (logs / audit trail) that shows traffic routing for Medix was confined to US-only hosts?

If we can get SOC2 + diagram + KMS confirmation by EOD Friday (2026-09-04) that would put us in a good position to move procurement.

Regards,
Daria
